docs.title: Market Analysis
docs.text:
An end-to-end financial analytics platform for stocks, cryptocurrencies, and ETFs.

Market Analysis combines automated market-data ingestion, cloud-hosted MySQL storage, PySpark transformations, Power BI reporting, and a natural-language analytics assistant powered by Groq.

The platform is designed to turn market data into accessible analysis: Python retrieves data from Yahoo Finance, structured records are stored in MySQL, analytical transformations support deeper exploration, and dashboards and an AI assistant expose insights to users.

docs.title: Main workflows
docs.text:
1. Retrieve market data from Yahoo Finance.
  2. Prepare structured datasets and load them into MySQL.
  3. Apply SQL and PySpark analytical transformations.
  4. Refresh Power BI dashboards from updated datasets.
  5. Allow users to ask market questions in natural language.
  6. Generate and execute SQL against the market database, then explain the returned results.

Start with the system overview Explore the data pipeline

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The platform includes a conversational assistant that lets users explore market data without manually writing SQL. The README describes a Groq-powered LLM integration and a natural-language-to-SQL workflow.

docs.title: Request lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI as React interface
    participant Agent as Groq LLM / SQL agent
    participant DB as Aiven MySQL
    User->>UI: Ask a market question
    UI->>Agent: Submit natural-language request
    Agent->>Agent: Generate SQL from database context
    Agent->>DB: Execute generated SQL
    DB-->>Agent: Query result
    Agent-->>UI: Explain result in natural language
    UI-->>User: Display insight and query

docs.title: Example questions
docs.text:
The README gives examples such as:

  • Which stock generated the highest return this month?
  • Compare Bitcoin and Ethereum performance over the last 90 days.
  • Which ETF has the lowest volatility?
  • What assets are showing bullish trends?
  • Show the top gainers and losers.
  • Identify unusual market movements.

docs.title: Grounding and safety considerations
docs.text:
A natural-language-to-SQL assistant should be treated as a database client, not as an independent source of market truth. Its answer depends on: - The records available in MySQL. - The schema and metadata supplied to the SQL-generation step. - The generated SQL and its execution result. - The date range and asset universe represented in the database.

For production use, generated SQL should be validated before execution, database credentials should have least-privilege access, and query execution should be read-only where possible. These are recommended safeguards; do not infer that every safeguard is already implemented.

docs.title: Python ingestion
docs.text: The ingestion layer retrieves financial data from Yahoo Finance through yFinance, prepares records, writes CSV datasets, and loads data into the MySQL database.

docs.title: MySQL on Aiven Cloud
docs.text: Aiven hosts the MySQL database so the data pipeline, web application, Power BI, and scheduled workflows can connect to a shared database service. The README describes SSL-encrypted connections and managed database capabilities.

docs.title: PySpark and SQL analytics
docs.text: PySpark supports transformations and aggregations over market datasets. SQL queries provide additional analytical views such as returns, volume, volatility, and asset comparisons.

docs.title: Power BI
docs.text: Power BI connects to the generated datasets and the hosted MySQL database to present market information through interactive dashboards.

docs.title: AI assistant
docs.text: The assistant uses Groq LLM integration to translate user questions into SQL, execute queries against market data, and explain the returned results in natural language.

docs.title: React web interface
docs.text: The React interface brings market dashboards and the conversational assistant into a browser-based experience.

docs.title: Architecture boundary
docs.text: The README describes the web backend as JavaScript and separately describes the Python data pipeline. It does not fully specify every internal web API boundary or the exact SQL-agent implementation. Those details should be verified in the corresponding source files before documenting endpoint-level behavior.

docs.title: Scheduled refresh with GitHub Actions
docs.text:
The project README describes a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the Python data pipeline on a schedule. Its example cron expression is:

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 18 * * 1-5'

The example runs at 18:00 UTC, Monday through Friday. It is an illustrative schedule in the README; it should not be interpreted as an exchange-calendar-aware market-close trigger.

The workflow example: 1. Checks out the repository. 2. Sets up Python. 3. Installs dependencies. 4. Runs python pipeline.py. 5. Supplies Aiven connection values from GitHub Secrets.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
The README identifies these secret names in its example:

  • AIVEN_HOST
  • AIVEN_PORT
  • AIVEN_USER
  • AIVEN_PASSWORD

Keep database credentials in GitHub Secrets or another secret manager. Do not commit credentials into source files, documentation examples, or frontend bundles.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
The README identifies Vercel as the web application deployment platform and Aiven as the managed MySQL host.

The project README contains placeholder demo URLs (your-project.vercel.app and a placeholder Loom video ID). Do not publish those as verified live links. Use the actual deployment URL only after confirming it from the deployment dashboard.

docs.title: Operational checklist
docs.text:
• Confirm Yahoo Finance access and data retrieval success.
  • Confirm the Aiven MySQL connection and SSL configuration.
  • Verify GitHub Actions workflow status and logs.
  • Check that generated CSV files are refreshed.
  • Validate that downstream Power BI refreshes have completed.
  • Verify that the AI assistant can access only the intended database operations.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The README describes the ingestion process as the following sequence:

  1. Python fetches current market data from Yahoo Finance.
  2. The pipeline writes the retrieved data to CSV files.
  3. Python creates the required MySQL tables.
  4. Data is loaded into the Aiven-hosted MySQL database.
  5. PySpark performs analytical transformations.
  6. Power BI reads Python-generated datasets and/or the MySQL database.
  7. Dashboard refreshes make updated market information available.

docs.title: Data destinations
docs.text: The project uses both CSV datasets and a MySQL database. CSV files support data exchange and dashboard workflows, while MySQL provides a shared structured store for application and analytics queries.

docs.title: Data quality considerations
docs.text:
Financial data can contain missing values, market-calendar gaps, symbol changes, and source-specific differences. A robust operational workflow should validate: - Symbol and asset-class identifiers. - Date/time consistency and market timezone assumptions. - Numeric price and volume fields. - Duplicate records for the same symbol and date. - Missing or incomplete upstream responses.

These are recommended validation checks; the README does not claim a particular implemented validation framework.

docs.title: MySQL on Aiven Cloud
docs.text:
The platform stores structured market data in MySQL hosted on Aiven Cloud. The README identifies connectivity from the web application, Power BI, the Python pipeline, and GitHub Actions.

The README also describes SSL-encrypted connections and managed database features such as backups and scalability. Actual availability and configuration depend on the Aiven service plan and deployment settings.

docs.title: SQL analytics
docs.text:
The project README includes examples of analytical questions and SQL patterns:

Analysis Example calculation Asset return Compare maximum and minimum close values Trading activity Aggregate volume by date Volatility Calculate standard deviation of close prices Average daily movement Compare close and open values Monthly performance Aggregate prices by month Asset category comparison Group by asset type

Example query from the project README:

SELECT symbol,
       ROUND(((MAX(close) - MIN(close)) / MIN(close)) * 100, 2) AS return_pct
FROM market_data
GROUP BY symbol
ORDER BY return_pct DESC;

This is an illustrative query included in the README. Its result depends on the selected date range and the exact schema/data loaded into market_data.

docs.title: PySpark analytics
docs.text:
The README lists PySpark transformations for daily returns, rolling averages, volume aggregation, volatility, monthly aggregation, ranking, and bullish/bearish filtering.

Example pattern:

df.withColumn(
    "daily_return",
    (col("Close") - col("Open")) / col("Open")
)

Window functions such as lag, dense_rank, and rolling aggregations can support time-series analysis. Confirm the actual DataFrame schema and window specification in the implementation before adapting examples.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: The repository archive includes separate areas for the Python data pipeline and React frontend, along with supporting analytics and dashboard assets. The exact directory structure can evolve; inspect the current repository before relying on fixed paths.

docs.title: Python pipeline setup
docs.text:
cd data_pipeline
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

The dependency file includes pandas, yfinance, SQLAlchemy, mysql-connector-python, and python-dotenv.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Provide Aiven database connection settings through environment variables as expected by the pipeline. The README's GitHub Actions example uses AIVEN_HOST, AIVEN_PORT, AIVEN_USER, and AIVEN_PASSWORD.

Never place production credentials in the repository or in client-side React environment variables that are bundled into public assets.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Checks Market data is missing Check symbol validity, upstream availability, and request logs Database connection fails Verify Aiven host, port, credentials, SSL settings, and network access Scheduled refresh did not run Inspect GitHub Actions schedule, workflow permissions, and run logs Power BI shows stale values Confirm pipeline completion and dataset refresh status AI assistant returns an incorrect result Inspect generated SQL, schema context, date filters, and query result Dashboard chart is empty Check the selected symbol, available date range, and API/database response

docs.title: Documentation boundary
docs.text: This guide reflects the project README and dependency manifest. Exact frontend commands, backend start commands, table definitions, and deployed environment values should be documented from the current source configuration rather than assumed.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Market Analysis addresses fragmented financial information by bringing stocks, cryptocurrency, and ETF data into a common analytics workflow. It combines a repeatable ingestion pipeline with database storage, analytical processing, dashboards, and natural-language querying.

docs.title: Asset coverage
docs.text:
The project README lists representative assets including:

  • Stocks: AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, NFLX, INTC, INFY, and F.
  • Cryptocurrencies: BTC, ETH, SOL, ADA, AVAX, LINK, and FIL.
  • ETFs: SPY, QQQ, SOXL, SOXS, IWM, EEM, and GDX.

The lists are examples rather than an exhaustive supported-universe specification.

docs.title: User-facing capabilities
docs.text:
• Market dashboards for stocks, crypto, and ETFs.
  • Historical price charts and timeframe selection.
  • Dark and light dashboard themes.
  • AI-powered natural-language questions about market data.
  • Export and analysis workflows using Python-generated datasets and Power BI.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
The repository includes a data_pipeline/requirements.txt file listing the Python ingestion dependencies:

cd data_pipeline
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

The listed packages are pandas, yfinance, SQLAlchemy, mysql-connector-python, and python-dotenv.

The repository also contains a React frontend. Follow its own package scripts and environment configuration for frontend development; do not assume a fixed development port or command without checking its package.json.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning Asset A financial instrument tracked by the platform ETF Exchange-traded fund yFinance Python library used to access Yahoo Finance market data OHLC Open, high, low, and close price fields Volume Number of units traded during a period Aiven Managed cloud data platform hosting the project's MySQL database PySpark Python API for Apache Spark data processing SQL agent Component that generates or uses SQL in response to user requests Natural-language-to-SQL Translating a human question into a database query Groq LLM Language-model service used by the assistant GitHub Actions Workflow automation service integrated with GitHub Power BI Business-intelligence platform for dashboards and reports Volatility Statistical measure of variation in asset prices or returns Drawdown Decline from a previous peak to a subsequent trough

docs.title: Role of Power BI
docs.text: Power BI provides the business-intelligence layer for visualizing the market datasets. The project README says Power BI connects to Python-generated datasets and the Aiven-hosted MySQL database.

docs.title: Dashboard categories
docs.text:
The README describes dedicated dashboard experiences for:

  • Stocks
  • Cryptocurrencies
  • Exchange-traded funds (ETFs)

docs.title: Documented dashboard interactions
docs.text:
• Scrollable asset/symbol sidebar.
  • Price charts for the selected instrument.
  • Current price, absolute change, and percentage change.
  • Timeframe selection, including 1Y, 3M, 5D, 5Y, and 6M.
  • Dark and light theme support.

docs.title: Refresh workflow
docs.text:
1. The scheduled or manually triggered Python pipeline retrieves updated market data.
  2. CSV datasets and MySQL records are updated.
  3. Power BI reads the updated data on its next refresh.

The README describes automatic refresh behavior. The exact Power BI refresh schedule and gateway configuration are environment-specific and should be verified in the deployed workspace.

docs.title: Integration overview
docs.text: The Python pipeline is the primary market-data ingestion path. MySQL acts as the shared structured data store. PySpark and SQL support analytical processing, Power BI presents visual reports, and the Groq-powered assistant offers conversational access to selected database insights.
